extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys, agents), patent examiners, judges, and advanced law students
extracted.subtask_description: Digest of U.S. patent-law propositions and procedural rules (abandonment, prosecution, pleadings, equity and law remedies, appeals, examination, amendments, drawings, accounts, etc.) with case citations illustrating each rule. Intended as a practitioner's reference for litigation and prosecution issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere conception vs abandonment to public
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere mental conception can be abandoned as to rival inventors, but only a completed invention can be abandoned to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case: Webster v. Sanford (1888), 44 O. G. 567. Distinguish rights vis-à-vis rival inventors from dedication/abandonment to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay before application not ipso facto abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay in applying for a patent is not ipso facto abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case: United States Electric Lighting Co. v. Consolidated Electric Light Co. (1888), 33 Fed. Rep. 869. However, laches in applying may defeat an earlier inventor in favor of a diligent later inventor (Hubel v. Dick (1886)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental use/sale not necessarily public use
rubrics_metrics.description: An experimental sale or use is not public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campbell v. City of New York (1888), 35 Fed. Rep. 504. Experimental use by inventor not public use even if profit derived, unless the use is mainly for profit and the experiment only incidental and public for >2 years before application (Smith & Griggs Mfg. Co. v. Sprague (1887), 123 U.S. 249).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use test: control, reservation, and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use put into public use without reserving rights, exercising control, or examining to test efficiency is not experimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Root v. Third Ave. R.R. Co. (1889), 37 Fed. Rep. 673. Burden rests on patentee to prove that a public use more than two years before application was experimental.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Two years before the application" meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: "Two years before the application" means before the application is filed in the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campbell v. City of New York (1888), 35 Fed. Rep. 504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of patent not a sale for abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment of a patent is not a sale of the invention nor regarded as public use/sale for abandonment purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: United States Electric Lighting Co. v. Consolidated Electric Light Co. (1888), 33 Fed. Rep. 869.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge/consent of inventor not required for public-use abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge and consent of the inventor are not necessary to an abandonment by public use under the Acts of 1836 and 1839; allegation of consent is surplusage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Andrews v. Hovey (1888), 124 U.S. 694; Campbell v. City of New York (1888), 35 Fed. Rep. 504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use under joint patent bars later sole patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Public use under a joint patent is a bar to a sole patent to one of the former joint patentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to claim may be abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patentee has full knowledge of all facts, a failure to claim may be an abandonment to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Huber v. N. O. Nelson Mfg. Co. (1889), 38 Fed. Rep. 830.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to claim described matter is abandonment unless timely steps taken
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to claim described matter is abandonment unless steps are taken to protect it by timely application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brush Electric Co. v. Fort Wayne Electric Light Co. (1889), 40 Fed. Rep. 826.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation in application for future patents improper
rubrics_metrics.description: Reservation in an application of matter to be covered by future patents is improper; inventor's right to a patent is independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Described but essentially distinct invention not dedicated
rubrics_metrics.description: A described invention essentially distinct from the one claimed and which ought not to have been mentioned is not dedicated to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of art in apparatus patent not dedication if later applied for
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of an art in a patent for apparatus does not dedicate the art to the public if a patent for it is applied for within two years from the date of the other patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eastern Paper Bag Co. v. Nixon (1888), 35 Fed. Rep. 752.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoning application does not abandon the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is not abandoned by abandoning the application, and an abandoned application is not open to the public until two years' public use or sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity parties: interest in proceeds may suffice
rubrics_metrics.description: A person having an interest in the proceeds of the suit but not in the patent need not be a party to a bill in equity for infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive-grantee must be joined with grantor in injunction suits
rubrics_metrics.description: The grantee of the exclusive right to make, use, and sell throughout the United States on payment of royalties must be joined as plaintiff with his grantor in a suit to enjoin infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clement Mfg. Co. v. Upson & Hall Co. (1889), 40 Fed. Rep. 471.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner/licensor/ licensee may join on multi-patent suits
rubrics_metrics.description: The sole owner of one patent may join with the licensor and exclusive licensee of another patent in a suit for an act which infringes both patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Huber v. Myers Sanitary Depot (1888), 34 Fed. Rep. 752.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court discretion on multifariousness of bill
rubrics_metrics.description: The court must determine, in its discretion, whether a bill is multifarious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singer Mfg. Co. v. Springfield Foundry Co. (1888), 34 Fed. Rep. 393.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of averment of interest by assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: An averment that the plaintiff became interested in the patent before bringing suit by assignments of which profert is made is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clement Mfg. Co. v. Upson & Hall Co. (1889), 40 Fed. Rep. 471.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill describing invention must have sufficient certainty
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill describing the invention without sufficient certainty is demurrable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wise v. Grand Avenue R. R. Co. (1888), 33 Fed. Rep. 277.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to count on additional or reissue patents allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: After decree for defendants the bill may be amended to count on an additional patent or to count on the reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Underwood v. Gerber (1889), 37 Fed. Rep. 796; Reay v. Berlin & Jones Envelope Co. (1887), 24 Blatch. 278.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plea cannot raise substantive defenses or infringement issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter of substantive defense cannot be urged on a plea; a plea in equity cannot raise the issue of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hendy v. Golden State & Miners' Iron Works (1888); Kom v. Wiebensch (1887), 33 Fed. Rep. 50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term expiration may be raised by plea in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The question whether the term of the patent has expired may be raised by plea in equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edison Electric Light Co. v. U. S. Electric Lighting Co. (1888), 35 Fed. Rep. 134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defence of non-patentability need not be in the answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The defense of non-patentability for want of inventive skill need not be set up in the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hendy v. Golden State & Miners' Iron Works (1888), 127 U.S. 370.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer may be amended to cover prior patents evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of the answer will be allowed to cover evidence of prior patents which have been treated as regularly in the case for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Babcock & Wilcox Co. v. Pioneer Iron Works (1888), 34 Fed. Rep. 338.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laches may be fatal to equity claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Laches of the plaintiff in equity may be fatal to his claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: No laches while actively enforcing claims in courts
rubrics_metrics.description: A plaintiff is not guilty of laches while enforcing his claims against infringers in general in the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: American Bell Telephone Co. v. Southern Telephone Co. (1888), 34 Fed. Rep. 795.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant cannot file cross-bill to enjoin plaintiff
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant cannot file a cross-bill to enjoin the plaintiff from infringing the defendant's patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McCormick Harvesting Mach. Co. v. Deering (1889), 47 O. G. 1222.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel must anticipate and be prepared for points from evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel are bound to anticipate and be prepared for every point that can be made on the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing limited; not for merely cumulative evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A rehearing will not be allowed on evidence already before the court and passed on adversely unless manifest error; rehearing will not be granted to enable defendants to take more evidence against the plaintiff's right to file a disclaimer if notice had been given, or to offer cumulative proof on comparative utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rogers v. Reissner (1888); Electrical Accumulator Co. v. Julien Electric Co. (1889), 39 Fed. Rep. 490.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening hearing for new Supreme Court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing may be opened and new evidence taken on the ground of a recent Supreme Court decision giving new views of the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campbell v. Mayor of New York (1888), 36 Fed. Rep. 260.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting of profits limited to pre-suit infringements
rubrics_metrics.description: An accounting of profits can be had only when the infringement took place before the suit was commenced; accounting must be limited to the time fixed by the plaintiff as the period of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marsh v. Nichols (1888), 128 U.S. 605; Creamer v. Bowers (1888), 35 Fed. Rep. 206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of claims not considered on accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: The validity of the claims of the patent cannot be considered on the accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skinner v. Vulcan Iron Works (1889), 39 Fed. Rep. 870.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's draft report objections must be raised early
rubrics_metrics.description: No objections to the final report will be considered unless they were urged against the draft report; accidental overlooking may sometimes allow later objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Celluloid Mfg. Co. v. Cellonite Mfg. Co. (1889), 40 Fed. Rep. 476.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reluctance to set aside master's report; facts vs law
rubrics_metrics.description: A master's report is to be set aside with almost as much reluctance as a jury verdict; conclusions on matters of fact are not departed from unless error or mistake clearly shown; matters of law may be objected to at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Welling v. La Ban (1888), 34 Fed. Rep. 40; Tilghman v. Proctor (1888), 125 U.S. 136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill of review time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill of review for errors on the face of the decree must be filed within two years from the date of the decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs entitlement when suing on multiple patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant who sues in equity on two patents and recovers on only one is entitled to costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schmid v. Scottle Mfg. Co. (1889), 37 Fed. Rep. 345.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court discretion on delivery up of infringing articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant will not be compelled to deliver up infringing articles to be destroyed when he acted in good faith and no further infringement is probable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: American Bell Telephone Co. v. Kitsell (1888), 35 Fed. Rep. 621.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action at law forbidden pending accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: A suit at law cannot be brought without leave of the courts pending an accounting, as the accounting may cover such infringements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive licensee status and right to sue
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusive license to make and sell throughout the United States on payment of royalties leaves legal title in the licensor, and he may sue third parties for infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration must allege no >2 years public use prior to filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The declaration must allege that the invention has not been in public use for more than two years before the application; denying public use 'with consent of the inventor' is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blessing v. Trageser Steam Copper Works (1888), 34 Fed. Rep. 763.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demurrer for non-patentability and novelty standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A demurrer for non-patentability will be sustained if the court can see the patent is void; a demurrer for non-patentability is sustained only when no question of fact can arise; demurrer for lack of novelty sustained only when device is clearly well-known and in common use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: West v. Rae (1887), 33 Fed. Rep. 45; Blessing v. Trageser; Eclipse Mfg. Co. v. Adkins (1888), 36 Fed. Rep. 554.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings follow local court forms; notice of special defenses not pleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings in patent cases follow forms employed in local courts; notice of special defenses is not a pleading and cannot be demurred to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Celluloid Mfg. Co. v. American Zylonite Co. (1888), 34 Fed. Rep. 744; Henry v. United States (1887).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial notice and evidence rules on novelty and utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may take judicial notice of want of novelty in clear cases; lack of invention must fairly appear or the patent will prevail; a patent is prima facie evidence of novelty and utility and places burden on challenger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ligowski Clay Pigeon Co. v. American Clay Bird Co. (1888); Kirk v. DuBois (1887), 33 Fed. Rep. 558; Frankfort Whiskey Process Co. v. Mill Creek Distilling Co. (1889).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original application admissible to show character of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The original application and its amendments are admissible to show the character of the actual invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidated Electric Light Co. v. McKeesport Light Co. (1889), 40 Fed. Rep. 21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting expert testimony: prefer fact-based testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Where opposing experts conflict, one stating facts within his knowledge and the other asserting a theory, the former will be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive testimony not disregarded because of improbability
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive testimony will not be disregarded because it is improbable that the same idea occurred to two persons independently at about the same time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret infringement must be proved by plaintiff
rubrics_metrics.description: An infringement carried on secretly must be proved by the plaintiff; plaintiff cannot rely solely on examining defendant or workmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other adjudged infringing devices admissible as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Other devices adjudged to be infringements may be offered in evidence to show that defendant's device is an infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alien and citizen patentees on same footing
rubrics_metrics.description: Alien and citizen patentees are on the same footing under U.S. law except as to fees and caveats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edison Electric Light Co. v. U. S. Electric Lighting Co. (1888), 35 Fed. Rep. 134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application petition must identify specification and obey rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition of the applicant must identify the specification, and the oath concerning foreign patents must be specific; application rules must be carefully observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application oath is evidence and may limit patent construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The application oath is evidence against the patentee and may limit the construction of his patent; an innocent false oath as to citizenship does not avoid the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worswick Mfg. Co. v. City of Kansas (1889), 38 Fed. Rep. 239; Tondeur v. Chambers (1889).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures: full Christian name required
rubrics_metrics.description: The full Christian name must be signed to the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second patent to same person for same invention unlawful
rubrics_metrics.description: After one patent has issued, a second patent to the same person for the same invention, though with broader claims, is unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidated Roller-Mill Co. v. Coombs (1889), 39 Fed. Rep. 25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of subsequent patent presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant of a subsequent patent to the same inventor raises a presumption that the later patent covers at least a patentable improvement on the former.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Putnam v. Keystone Bottle Stopper Co. (1889), 38 Fed. Rep. 234.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign narrow patent does not preclude broader domestic patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign patent with narrow claims does not prevent obtaining a domestic patent for a broader invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article produced necessarily by patented machine not separately patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: An article which is the necessary product of a machine already patented is not the subject-matter of a patent if it can be made only by that machine; but if producible by other methods, it may be considered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process patent not available after article patented
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent cannot be obtained for the process of making an article after a patent has been granted for the article as made by that process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mosler Safe and Lock Co. v. Mosler (1888), 127 U.S. 354.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early application may yield patent despite later improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be granted on an earlier application though since it was filed other patents have been granted on subsequent applications for improvements on the subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Several applications for same indivisible subject-matter cannot be entertained
rubrics_metrics.description: Several applications for the same indivisible subject-matter cannot be entertained; each application must be clearly distinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of application only when total want of interdependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Division should not be required unless there is such a total want of interdependence as to render the inventions absolutely independent and distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder: combination and elements may be joined unless Office classification opposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A combination and its elements, a combination and improvements on its parts, and a machine and parts not recognized in the arts as distinct devices may be joined in one application unless opposed to Office classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separable element already in general use cannot be joined
rubrics_metrics.description: A separable element already in general use cannot be joined with the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte La Borde (1888), 44 O. G. 700.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere improvements not affecting essence cannot be joined
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere improvements on old elements of a combination not affecting the essence of the element cannot be joined with the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements may be joined where they act together to single result
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more elements of a machine may be joined where one depends on and acts with the other to produce a single result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and apparatus may be joined when mutually dependent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the apparatus cannot operate without performing the process, and the process requires apparatus substantially identical, no division should be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and product/apparatus require separate applications when separable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a process and its product or apparatus can separately exist they require separate applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent covers only one invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent can cover but one invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings cannot expand patent beyond specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings cannot make the patent cover a different invention from that described in the specification, either on reissue or by disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hailes v. Albany Stove Co. (1887), 123 U.S. 682.

rubrics_metrics.name: New figures cannot be added after filing without permission
rubrics_metrics.description: New figures cannot be added to the drawings after filing without express permission from the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lettering of drawings and specification must correspond
rubrics_metrics.description: The lettering of the drawings and specification must correspond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where none of combination elements are new, patentees limited to form shown in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where none of the elements of a combination are new or claimed separately and other similar combinations are in use, patentee is limited to the form of the elements shown by his drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heine Safety Boiler Co. v. Smith F.W.H. & P. Co. (1889), 47 O. G. 1634.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must satisfy Patent Office invention operative and useful
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must satisfy the Patent Office that his invention is operative and useful as well as new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte De Baussett (1888), 43 O. G. 1583.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office duty to assist applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the duty of the Patent Office to see that the applicant obtains a patent for whatever patentable subject-matter his application covers and to act as his friend, advising how to meet objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte Donovan (1888), 44 O. G. 698; Ex parte Burt (1889).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require definite, intelligible claims but not hinder appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner can require that claims be definite and intelligible, but cannot in any manner hinder the applicant from obtaining his full rights on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment cannot introduce matter not substantially disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment cannot introduce matter not substantially disclosed in the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment covering distinct invention cannot be received
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment covering a distinct invention cannot be received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment proposing claim not identical with disclosed invention should be admitted to allow appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment proposing a claim not identical with the invention already disclosed or with a part thereof should be admitted and rejected so an appeal may be taken; but if it covers an essentially distinct invention requiring division it should not be received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's oath about amendment not conclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant's oath that matter claimed by an amendment was part of the original invention is not conclusive; the Office may inspect the whole application to determine the question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim once erased should not be restored by amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim once erased should not be restored by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized figure addition erased
rubrics_metrics.description: A figure added in good faith to a drawing on file without the Office's permission will be erased.

rubrics_metrics.name: After second rejection applicant cannot amend as matter of right
rubrics_metrics.description: After a second rejection the applicant cannot amend as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late amendment nearly two years after rejection requires explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presented nearly two years after rejection will not be received unless the delay is explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application cannot be withdrawn from issue for amendment except to prevent irreparable injury
rubrics_metrics.description: An application cannot be withdrawn from issue for purposes of amendment unless irreparable injury would otherwise result; allowed application may be withdrawn if irreparable injury would result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte Page (1888); Ex parte Myers (1889), 49 O. G. 131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant bound by prior refusal to adopt examiner-suggested amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant, refusing to adopt an amendment suggested by the examiner, is defeated and years afterward applies for leave to make such amendment, he is bound by the prior refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections must be full and positive to be appealed
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection to be the subject of an appeal must be a full and positive rejection, not a mere objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: All patentability questions should be acted on before appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: All questions relating to patentability should be acted on before appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal routes: oath, merits, functional claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal from rejection for want of a proper oath lies to the examiners-in-chief; an objection to a claim as functional is not a rejection and appeal to examiners-in-chief does not lie; functional claims are necessarily indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte Boyer (1889); Ex parte Barrett (1888).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal on merits goes to examiners-in-chief, not Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection on the merits must be followed by an appeal to the examiners-in-chief, not by a petition to the Commissioner for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination vs aggregation: substance question and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a device is a combination or an aggregation is a question of substance; appeal lies to the examiners-in-chief. A claim for an aggregation should be rejected and appeal allowed instead of ordering a division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte Baker (1889); Ex parte Willcox (1888).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners-in-chief do not decide division questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of division does not fall within the cognizance of the examiners-in-chief; their recommendation as to it is unwarranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division ordering: examiner must give full information
rubrics_metrics.description: In ordering a division between process and product the examiner must give the applicant all the information on which he bases his judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may waive cross-reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may waive his requirement for cross-references between pending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications treated same re prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional applications are treated as the same proceeding with reference to prior use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frankfort Whiskey Process Co. v. Mill Creek Distilling Co. (1889), 37 Fed. Rep. 533.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavoidable delay does not abandon application
rubrics_metrics.description: Unavoidable delay in prosecuting an application does not abandon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ligowski Clay Pigeon Co. v. American Clay Bird Co. (1888), 34 Fed. Rep. 328.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application suspension >2 years at applicant's request abandons it
rubrics_metrics.description: An application cannot be suspended at the request of the applicant for more than two years without abandoning it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Last action must be regular/legal to preserve application
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'last action' of the Patent Office to preserve or obtain the right must be regular and legal, not an irregular step taken by applicant and refused recognition by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith but unimportant amendments can save application
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed in good faith but not important in character can save the application from abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal amendment may be accepted conditionally to save application
rubrics_metrics.description: An informal amendment may be received by the Office to save the application from abandonment, on condition it be subsequently made to comply with the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not removing objections do not prevent abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments not removing objections nor changing the application's status in the Office are not sufficient prosecution to prevent abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second original application after abandonment allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: A second original application for the same invention can be filed after the first is abandoned by two years' neglect to renew after forfeiture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoned application not a bar to subsequent patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandoned application is no bar to a subsequent patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoned/rejected application cannot be cited as reference
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandoned or rejected application cannot be cited as a reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of abandoned cases furnished for evidence but inspection motions denied generally
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of abandoned cases in the Patent Office must be furnished on application if needed for evidence, but motions to inspect such cases generally will be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte Fowler (1889), 49 O. G. 562; United States v. Hall (1889), 48 O. G. 1263.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney may obtain mandamus for copies of abandoned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney at law may obtain mandamus against the Commissioner in his own name to procure copies of abandoned applications from the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: United States v. Hall (1889), 48 O. G. 1263.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuations are continuation only if cover same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are not continuous unless they cover the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: New application at suggestion of Office considered continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application filed at the suggestion of the Patent Office is a continuation of the old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Tooth Crown Co. v. Richmond (1887), 24 Blatch. 223.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executor-filed application considered continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application filed by the executor of a deceased applicant is a continuation of the former application and has the same status in the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant cannot forfeit and renew at option
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant has no right to forfeit an application and file a renewal at his option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed application cannot be withheld when unobjectionable
rubrics_metrics.description: An allowed application cannot be withheld when neither reference, publication, public use, nor interference can be urged against it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaust administrative appeals before equity bill to obtain patent
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte case in the Patent Office, remedies by appeal must be exhausted before a bill in equity to obtain the patent can be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary should not be party to bill to obtain patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary should not be made a party to a bill to obtain a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: On appeal awarding patent by priority, patentability may be raised
rubrics_metrics.description: On an appeal from a decree granting a patent to one of two rival inventors on sole ground of priority, the defeated party may raise the question of patentability and the Supreme Court may decide it.
